title: Author + implement PROP-NNN: investigate why PROP-076 pre-push lint gate is being silently skipped by decider; harden invocation (likely via git hook structural enforcement)
background:
Tinker's run at 2026-06-06T05-04 (commit 58b47ae1) discovered the actual driver behind the recurring PROP-059 critical alarms — and it's NOT what the operator suspected. The original directive (DIRECTIVE-20260605-001) was filed assuming integrity's filter was out of sync with the lint gate; tinker's forensics showed integrity's §7h has correctly recognized `audit_grandfathered` since 2026-05-26 (commit 5ffd21cc). The real bug is upstream:

**PROP-076's pre-push lint gate (`monitor/scripts/lint-close-records.js`) was SKIPPED on 3 decider pushes in 2 days.** Per the tinker report's [major] finding:

  - commit `38deae25` (2026-06-04T13:18Z) — ISS-2571..2577 closed without verification_pattern or audit_grandfathered
  - commit `f52d3ae0` (2026-06-05T01:16Z) — ISS-2579/2580 closed without either
  - commit `196dde8d` (2026-06-05T09:13Z) — ISS-2587 closed without either

Each of these landed decider-prefixed close-records with neither verification_pattern nor audit_grandfathered set — the exact shape `lint-close-records.js` is designed to exit-1 on. **The lint gate did not block.** This is the structural defense PROP-076 was meant to be.

Pattern parallel — this is the SAME bug class as the PROP-074 saga (LLM agent silently skipping a multi-step prompt action). For PROP-074 we tried six prompt-level iterations before architectural separation via dome-mirror finally fixed it. The lesson from that saga: structural enforcement beats prompt-level enforcement every time, because the LLM can be cajoled into skipping any line of prompt but cannot bypass git's own hook machinery.

The lint gate's invocation site is documented in `monitor/prompts/reference/decider-patches-and-selfapply.md` (per PROP-076's deploy). Three suspected failure modes:

  H1 — LLM skip-by-omission: the bash block invoking `node monitor/scripts/lint-close-records.js` is in the prompt's middle position and the LLM pattern-matches it as commentary rather than action. Same shape as PROP-074's Step 4c skip.

  H2 — Conditional invocation: the lint is gated on some condition (e.g., 'invoke only if commits touched closed-issues.json') and the condition logic has a hole. Decider's close-record commits sometimes batch with other writes and the check misses.

  H3 — Exit-1 not actually blocking: the lint runs and exits 1 but the surrounding bash either masks the exit code (`|| true`, `2>/dev/null`, similar) or the next bash invocation pushes anyway. Lint output may be visible in run logs as a 'warning' rather than a hard block.

The fix direction operator pre-approves is **structural enforcement via git hook**, mirroring PROP-074's lesson. Specifically: install a `pre-push` git hook in decider's clone setup that invokes `lint-close-records.js`. If the hook exits non-zero, git refuses the push. This is enforced by git itself; the LLM cannot bypass it short of removing the hook (which would be detectable).

operator_decision.rationale: Three documented bypasses in two days of a discipline-critical gate. PROP-074's saga proved that prompt-level enforcement of multi-step bash actions is unreliable in the face of LLM pattern-matching variability. Git hooks are enforced by git itself, not by LLM compliance, and run at a known well-defined moment (pre-push) regardless of where the LLM left the bash interpreter. This is the architecturally-correct solution that PROP-076 should have shipped with from day one.

requested_work: Step 1 — Forensic diagnosis. Read `monitor/prompts/reference/decider-patches-and-selfapply.md` to locate the existing PROP-076 lint gate invocation block. For each of the 3 bypass commits (38deae25, f52d3ae0, 196dde8d), pull the commit's stdout/stderr from decider's latest-decider-summary.txt or run report if available. Determine which of H1/H2/H3 is the dominant failure mode (may be multiple). Document in PROP-NNN's diagnosis section.

Step 2 — Author `monitor/tinker/proposals/PROP-NNN-lint-gate-structural-enforcement.json` (next free PROP-NNN; PROP-080 likely). Required sections: title, problem statement citing this directive + the 3 bypass commits + the diagnosis findings from Step 1, proposed fix (the pre-push hook), Q-OPs if any, verification_pattern (grep + actual simulation of the hook against the 3 bypass scenarios), files_touched list, estimated_loc.

Step 3 — Implement the pre-push hook. Operator pre-approves the following design directions; tinker should pick the cleanest:
  (a) PREFERRED: Add hook installation to decider's clone-setup step in monitor/prompts/reference/decider-patches-and-selfapply.md. Right after the clone is created (or refreshed each run), `cp monitor/scripts/lint-close-records.js .git/hooks/pre-push && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-push` — or a small wrapper script that invokes lint-close-records.js. Every push triggers the hook automatically. Simplest; no prompt drift risk.
  (b) Alternative: A dedicated install-hooks.sh that runs at decider's pre-flight setup. Slightly more LOC but cleaner separation.
  (c) Alternative: Move the lint invocation from prompt-level bash to a Node wrapper invoked AROUND the git push command (decider already shells out for git push; wrap that shell-out). LOC parity with (a) but invocation is more visible in decider's logic.
  Operator preference: (a) for surgical-fix-with-structural-property. The hook IS the gate; decider can't accidentally skip it.

Step 4 — Validation: simulate each of the 3 bypass scenarios (commits 38deae25 / f52d3ae0 / 196dde8d). For each: replay the commit's content into a test clone, install the hook per the new design, attempt `git push`, verify the hook fires AND exits non-zero AND git refuses the push. Document the simulation result in PROP-NNN's verification section. Operator wants explicit evidence the new design blocks all 3 historical bypass shapes.

Step 5 — Tinker self-applies per the PROP-076/077/078/079 pattern: write proposal, implement same run if total LOC <100 across decider prompt + (any) install script + (any) hook wrapper, verification simulation passes. Hold for operator review if a Q-OP arises that isn't pre-answered in Step 3.

Step 6 — Keep PROP-076's lint script (`monitor/scripts/lint-close-records.js`) unchanged unless Step 1 surfaces a real bug in the filter logic. The script's design is correct; only the invocation point is broken.

Step 7 — Lifecycle: flip PROP-NNN.json status='implemented' with implementation_commit/at/run. Flip this directive to status='completed' with prop_id_implemented set. Update PROP-076 status note to reference the new hook-based enforcement as the structural backstop (do NOT mark PROP-076 superseded — it's still the canonical filter spec; PROP-NNN just ships the structural enforcement layer).

Step 8 — Manually copy edited prompt + (any) install script + (any) hook wrapper to FUSE so decider's next session-bootstrap picks up the new design. dome-mirror will propagate within ~30 min on its :30 cron.

Step 9 — Operator follow-up reminder in PROP-NNN's post-deployment plan: tinker (or operator) should canary on the next 2-3 decider runs. Expected: zero new ISSs of this class on integrity's daily audits. If a 4th bypass shows up in coming days, the hook design is wrong or the LLM is finding a path around it — escalate immediately.
non_goals: Do NOT change PROP-076's lint script logic (the filter is correct; only the invocation point is broken).

Do NOT touch integrity's PROP-059 §7h audit. It worked correctly throughout (fired ISS-2581/2594 when violations actually existed). PROP-079 from this morning aligned the prompt verbiage; no further change needed.

Do NOT remove the existing prompt-level lint invocation from decider-patches-and-selfapply.md. Belt-and-suspenders: keep the prompt-level call as a layer-1 defense (catches violations earlier in the run) AND add the hook as layer-2 (catches them at push time regardless of prompt drift). Cost is one extra `node ...` call when both fire; benefit is the hook IS the actual block.
Do NOT scope to other lint surfaces (e.g., adding hooks for verification_pattern checks on workspace-sync's pushes). Stay focused on decider's close-record pushes for this PROP.

Do NOT block on retroactive cleanup of the 3 bypassed commits — they're already integrated, the close-records are already in closed-issues.json, integrity already caught and re-fired the criticals. Forward-looking enforcement is the work.

expected_output: (1) monitor/tinker/proposals/PROP-NNN-lint-gate-structural-enforcement.json with status='implemented'. (2) Edit to monitor/prompts/reference/decider-patches-and-selfapply.md (or monitor/prompts/decider.md) installing the pre-push hook per design (a). (3) Optionally: a small install-hooks.sh or hook wrapper if the inline cp+chmod is too messy. (4) PROP-NNN's verification section documenting the simulation result for all 3 bypass scenarios. (5) This directive at status='completed'. (6) FUSE-synced files.
estimated_effort: ~45-60 min Opus. Forensic diagnosis (Step 1, ~15 min) is the longest piece. Proposal authoring (Step 2, ~15 min). Implementation (Steps 3, 5) is short (~10 min, ~20-30 lines of prompt edit + maybe a 5-line hook wrapper). Simulation validation (Step 4, ~15 min). Lifecycle (Steps 7-8, ~10 min).
priority_note: HIGH — structural defense being silently bypassed. Every day this isn't fixed risks new same-class violations + alarm fatigue from integrity re-firing the same critical. Worth shipping in the next 1-2 tinker runs.
